items.title: Charlie Love Interview, 1959-12-09
items.q: At that time when I was practicing with him he played a valve trombone.

ctx.x: Williams' brother played the bass in the band and George Lewis. A fella in the name of Buddy Brunson. That man had the funniest lip I ever seen. I don't know what kind of trombone that he had. An E flat tenor trombone or something. A high one, a little one. Yeah. With the valve. With the valve. And he didn't know even how to tune but he could play it. You know what he'd do? He'd sound the air on the violin you know. And he'd finger any one of them valves, and he'd be flat that way he'd blow it up. He'd say, and…
I want to ask a little bit about Vincent again. How did he play? Did he ever take the slide trombone later? Do you remember?

At that time when I was practicing with him he played a valve trombone. But he could play that thing. He used to take a solo on it you know. Was he a good musician? Could he read and all? Yeah he could read right now. I hadn't started reading then when he was reading. I used to wish that I was great like him. And finally I got out of the business. My cousin named Brittany Henrietta, her husband was a bass horn player you know. He the one that taught Eddie Jackson. And he told me where to go to to get some good…
